provenance: Prepared, source-checked demonstration answers. A hit is not a live model generation.
matching: Exact listed aliases, matching story and source hashes, and [from_seconds, until_seconds) question-time window. Available on the phone and own-player TV. Otherwise use the live pipeline.
limits: No fuzzy matching, cross-title substitutions, follow-up/thread substitutions or fixed catch-up recaps. TV lists only source-checked examples already available at the frozen question time. A prepared hit is not live generation.

requests: I missed that line. What does sit still mean?
I am grandma. What does sit still mean?
entries.answer: “Sit still” means stay in one place without moving. The caption does not say why.

visual.description: A schematic person settles once above a marked place, illustrating staying in one place without moving. It does not identify the caption's speaker.

requests: I got distracted. What did I miss?
I missed that. What did Arun say?
entries.answer: Arun just explained that he made the old kite with Maya’s mother when she was Maya’s age.

visual.description: Two labeled people, Arun and Maya's mother, connect to a kite. The connectors settle into place to show that they made it together.

entries.answer: “Mend” means repair something broken. Arun suggests using a patch to repair the torn kite.

visual.description: A yellow patch settles over a tear in a schematic kite. It explains Arun's proposed repair, not a repair already completed in the film.

entries.situation: Either person needs longer to understand
requests: Explain why he kept the kite more simply.
Why did Arun keep the old kite?
Why did he keep the kite?
entries.answer: Arun kept the kite because he made it with Maya’s mother. The old kite connects him to her.

visual.description: A schematic kite connects Arun with Maya's mother. The connectors settle into place, explaining the kite's established family connection without inventing an emotion.

entries.answer: At a teammate’s pass, an attacker beyond both the ball and second-last opponent in the opponents’ half is in an offside position. Active involvement makes it an offence.
